request.input_head:
Here are our documents.

=== Notes ===
Sample (fictional)

KETTLE LANE YOUTH THEATRE
Board meeting notes, October 21, 2026
Present: Owen Calloway (chair), Dela Marchetti (executive director), Priya Haldane (treasurer), Teo Brask (development), Hannah Voss (board)

Item 3: Reade Fund pitch

Teo reported that Ruth Ellingsen, program officer at the Tamsin Reade Fund for Rural Arts, invited us to send a short deck before their December committee meeting. She asked specifically about the eastern county touring gap.

Owen asked for a deck that requests $45,000 from the Reade Fund to close the gap on the $68,500 Eastern County touring company. Priya confirmed the $23,500 already in hand: $12,000 projected touring fees and $11,500 from the County Arts Council rural access fund.

Deadline: draft to Owen and Dela by November 13. Final goes to Ruth Ellingsen by November 20, 2026.

Instructions agreed for the deck:

1. Lead with the eastern county schools, not with our history. The 11 requests we turned down and the four of five schools with no arts teacher beyond music should be up front.
2. Use only FY2026 results from the annual report. The 3,400 additional students is an estimate and must be labeled as one.
3. Keep the caveat on the confidence survey (41 to 74 percent). Hannah: "If we drop the caveat, Ruth will find it in the report and we lose her trust." Do not present it as proof we caused the change.
4. No student photos and no last names. Wren's quote may be used with first name

response.draft:
Slide 1: Closing the Eastern County Touring Gap
Kettle Lane Youth Theatre | Ambry Falls
A proposal to the Tamsin Reade Fund for Rural Arts
Request: $45,000 to launch a second touring company in eastern Ambry County
Company start: January 2027

Slide 2: Eastern County Schools Are Asking. We Have Had to Say No.
In FY2026 we turned down 11 performance requests from eastern county schools
Four of the five eastern county schools we visit have no arts teacher on staff beyond music (Ambry County 2025 survey)
The drive runs up to 70 minutes each way
The reason we said no: one van and one touring cast

Slide 3: What Schools Already Get from Us
The Weathervane: a 40-minute, three-actor show about a girl who stops speaking after her family moves
Each show is followed by a 20-minute workshop led by the actors
FY2026: 31 performances in 14 schools
6,820 students reached in grades 3 through 8
Five of those 14 schools are in the eastern half of the county

Slide 4: The Plan: A Second Touring Company for the East
A touring company just for eastern county schools, starting with the spring 2027 semester
20 additional school visits in eastern Ambry County
An estimated 3,400 more students reached (estimate)
A follow-up workshop at every school
A new companion show for grades 6 through 8, alongside The Weathervane
An outside evaluation partner built into the budget

Slide 5: What Our FY2026 Results Show, and What They Don't
After-school student survey: "I feel confident speaking in front of my class at school"
September: 41 percent agreed. May: 74 percent agreed.
Limits: the answers are self-reported and there is no comparison group
We cannot say how much of the change came from us and how much from a year of growing up
Only 97 of 142 students completed both surveys; students who left may differ from those who stayed
A firmer measure: 83 percent of eligible students re-enrolled (98 of 118)
Waitlist for the 13-to-17 ensemble: 19 names in August

Slide 6: In a Student's Words
"I used to eat lunch in the library so nobody would talk to me. Now I'm the one who shows the new kids where the stage door is."
Wren, age 13, at the end-of-year circle, May 2026

Slide 7: The Ask: $45,000
Eastern County touring company budget: $68,500
Two touring teaching artists (school year): $44,000
Second van lease and fuel: $9,600
Production for the new companion show: $8,900
Outside evaluation partner: $6,000
Already in hand: $23,500
Projected touring fees from new schools (sliding scale, about $600 per visit): $12,000
Ambry County Arts Council rural access fund (approved September 2026): $11,500
Remaining gap: $45,000
We are asking the Tamsin Reade Fund to close that gap so the company can start in January 2027

Slide 8: A Well-Run Organization Ready to Grow
FY2026 expenses: $412,600. Revenue: $416,200. Operating surplus: $3,600 added to our cash reserve
About 81 percent of spending went to programs
61 percent of after-school students (87 of 142) received full or partial tuition aid; no student was turned away for cost
Support from 312 individual donors, the Halvorsen Family Foundation, and the Ambry County Arts Council
FY2027 evaluation: an outside evaluator, teacher ratings at two partner schools, and tracking of students who do not finish the year
Kettle Lane Youth Theatre | The Granary, 2nd Floor | Ambry Falls
